Scope & Objective: The 19th Special Forces Group (Airborne) requires contractor support to execute a comprehensive, 3-day/2-night CORE Family Resiliency Event for 20–25 military families (70–80 total participants). In direct support of the Preservation of the Force and Family (POTFF) initiative, this event will utilize an immersive outdoor camping environment in Utah to deliver evidence-based resiliency training, fostering readiness across the Body, Mind, Spirit, and Family pillars. 2. Professional Training & Credentials: The contractor shall provide credentialed Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to deliver objective

onals ensures a neutral environment free from military chain-of-command dynamics. The contractor must provide documented evidence of the following credentials prior to award: Staff Role Minimum Required Credentials Mental Health & Counseling Active state licensure (LMFT, LCSW, LPC) OR a Ph.D. in Psychology, Kinesiology, or Health Science. Outdoor Leadership Master's or Doctorate degree in Recreation Administration, Outdoor Leadership, Kinesiology, or a closely related ﬁeld. Safety & Field Staff Current Wilderness First Responder (WFR) or Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certiﬁcation, alongside CPR/AED. 3. Venue & Environmental Requirements: To maximize training effectiveness and remove the distractions of daily civilian-military life, the event must be conducted in an isolated, high-country outdoor adventure setting in Utah. The shared challenges of basecamp setup and outdoor navigation are required curriculum components to build team cohesion. Requirement Area Speciﬁcation Geographic Boundary The venue, campsite, and all training grounds must be located strictly within the state of Utah. Facilities Must include a headquarters cabin for command staff, a secure Family Basecamp area, instructional/dining areas with tables and chairs, and adequate parking. Sust

Facilities Must include a headquarters cabin for command staff, a secure Family Basecamp area, instructional/dining areas with tables and chairs, and adequate parking. Sustainment Continuous access to clean, potable water (for drinking, cooking, and hygiene) and functional, sanitary toilet facilities sized for 70–80 personnel. 4.
